meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The test was a piece of cake.
origin: Its exact origin is unclear. It is often linked to the idea that a slice of cake is easy to eat.

wrong_meanings.meaning: a dessert that is served at a party
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of 'cake', not the idiomatic meaning.
This is the opposite: the idiom means something is very easy.
The idiom has nothing to do with money; it describes how easy something is.

explanation: 'Piece of cake' is an informal idiom used when something is very easy to do. It does not refer to real cake.
